_doc: The shared universe list. A series or book belongs to a fictional universe ONLY where that says something the series name does not already say.
_home: catalog-platform/data/universes.json — the ONE copy, moved here from library_catalog/data/universes.json on 2026-08-11. Both catalogs read this path; neither keeps a copy in git. ⚠️ This makes catalog-platform a CODE dependency of library_catalog and audiobook_catalog, not a docs repo. Deleting or moving this file breaks their builds.
_scope: ⚠️ This list is SHARED BY BOTH CATALOGS and is not library_catalog data. It is keyed on series + author, which both sides can compute, because the same series exists in both collections under different rows and often in only one of them. Do not copy it into either catalog; a copy is how two lists drift. A build may materialise a gitignored copy as a build artifact (library_catalog does), but nothing tracked in git may hold a second version of these decisions.

_decided.canonicalNames: The owner's spellings win. 'Cosmere' normalises to 'The Cosmere'. The model tends to answer 'Arand multiverse'; that renames to 'Runnerverse'. The machine-readable form of this rule is the top-level `canonicalNames` map below; this sentence is the reasoning, that map is what the validator enforces.
_decided.confidence: high applies automatically; medium and low go to the owner. Measured on a 15-case probe: 13 right, 0 false positives.
_decided.provenance: Every entry records how it was decided — seed (hand-curated), human (owner confirmed), llm (proposed). A machine guess and a confirmed fact must stay distinguishable, following decided_how, cover_status and read_state_how.
_decided.whyAFileAndNotATable: ~33 series and ~13 book overrides, changing maybe monthly. This is reference data, not user data. A file puts the DECISIONS under version control — including the refusals, which is where most of the value is — and costs nothing, because a consumer can hold the whole list in memory and answer 'show me all Cosmere books' without a query. The audiobook side is a Python static build that cannot reach D1 at all, so a table would have needed an export step and a second copy anyway.

_theHardPart: ⚠️ A series→universe mapping is NOT sufficient, and this was found before spending anything on the API. Two real counterexamples in this collection, from opposite directions: 'Secret Projects' is a MIXED series — Tress, Yumi, The Sunlit Man and Isles of the Emberdark are Cosmere, The Frugal Wizard's Handbook is not — so a series-level answer would be wrong for one of five. And Arand's Otherlife / Selfless Hero Trilogy carries NO series value at all, so a series-keyed lookup misses it entirely. Both cases need per-book overrides, which also means the auto-assign-on-add path cannot read the series and stop.

_lookup.order: Both consumers MUST resolve in this order, and data/universes.fixtures.json pins it: (1) a bookExclusions title match returns NO universe and stops — an exclusion beats every other signal; (2) a bookOverrides title match returns that universe; (3) a series match against a universe's `series` list returns that universe; (4) otherwise no universe. `notSeries` never returns a universe, it only records a deliberate refusal for that universe.
_lookup.whyExclusionsFirst: The Frugal Wizard's Handbook and Lux - A Texas Reckoners Novel both sit next to titles that would otherwise sweep them in. Checking exclusions last would make the answer depend on which rule happened to fire first.
_lookup.matching: Titles and series are compared after normalising: lowercase, curly apostrophes folded to straight, whitespace collapsed, trimmed. ⚠️ Curly-apostrophe folding is load-bearing — the Frugal Wizard row in site/catalog.csv carries U+2019.
_lookup.exactTitlesOnly: ⚠️ Title matching is EXACT after normalising, never prefix or substring. A row whose title carries a subtitle — measured example: 'Isles of the Emberdark - A Cosmere Novel Secret Projects, Book 5' in the audiobook catalog — will NOT match the override 'Isles of the Emberdark'. That is deliberate. Substring matching would make 'Elantris' match 'The Hope of Elantris'. Rows with damaged titles are fixed in the owning catalog's corrections layer (audiobook_catalog scripts/catalog_overrides.json), not by loosening the match here.

_pinnedCanonicalNames._why: ⚠️ The owner's two explicit spelling decisions, asserted as ANSWERS. Validation checks these separately from canonicalNames because internal consistency is not enough: renaming 'The Cosmere' to 'Cosmere' and updating every alias to match would leave the map perfectly consistent while quietly reversing the decision. These two lines are what make that a failure instead of a clean diff. Adding a pin is an owner decision; the CLI never writes here.

canonicalNames._note: Lowercased-and-normalised alias → the owner's canonical spelling. Shape follows audiobook_catalog scripts/catalog_overrides.json `canonical_series`, which does the same job for series names. ⚠️ Two entries are required by the owner's rule and are not cosmetic: 'cosmere' → 'The Cosmere' and 'arand multiverse' → 'Runnerverse'. 'divine dungeon universe' and 'zodiac academy universe' are evidenced by this file's own CAL Verse and Solaria `naming` notes, which record that both were named for the shared world rather than for one series inside it. No other alias is guessed; add one only with a reason.
canonicalNames._namespace: ⚠️ These are UNIVERSE names, not series names. 'Cosmere' is also a stray SERIES value on two library works — that is the data problem recorded under The Cosmere `notes`, and it is a different namespace from this map.

universes.name: The Cosmere
universes.notes: ⚠️ 'Cosmere' and 'The Cosmere' currently exist as SERIES values on two different works — a universe masquerading as a series, spelled two ways. Those two works need a real series (or none) once this lands. Reckoners and Skyward are the same author and deliberately excluded; Skyward is the Cytoverse.
universes.confirmed: Owner approved 2026-08-11, series and book-level, after reviewing all 19 unclassified titles.

bookOverrides.title: Elantris
bookOverrides.why: Sel — an audio row filed with no series, duplicating the Elantris series entry

bookOverrides.title: Fires of December
bookOverrides.why: ⚠️ Standalone with NO series, narrated by Hoid. Publisher copy via Books-A-Million (9781250462657) calls it 'a standalone Cosmere novel'; the owner's Hoid's Storybook Collection pledge corroborates it — chasmfiend plush, The Girl Who Looked Up figurine, Hoid's Flute. THE example of the owner's own rule: in a universe, not connected by series.

bookExclusions.title: The Frugal Wizard’s Handbook for Surviving Medieval England
bookExclusions.why: ⚠️ Secret Projects 2 — the one of five that is NOT Cosmere. This single row is the proof that a series-level mapping cannot work.

bookExclusions.title: Firstborn / Defending Elysium
bookExclusions.why: ⚠️ An OMNIBUS, not a data error — corrected by the owner. It is a real published two-novella volume: one file (firstborn_defendingelysium.epub), and the audiobook catalog's own description enumerates its contents as bullets, one of which reads '(from the world of Skyward)'. NEITHER novella is Cosmere. Belongs in edition.collects (migration 0060), the same shape as the White Sand omnibus — not split into two works.

bookExclusions.title: Lux - A Texas Reckoners Novel
bookExclusions.why: Reckoners spin-off. Also note 'Texas Reckoners series' is a separate series value from 'Reckoners' — likely the same thing split in two.

universes.name: Runnerverse
universes.evidence: Fostering Faust is credited to BOTH names in the owner's own data, which is direct evidence the two identities are one author rather than an outside assertion.

bookOverrides.title: Otherlife Dreams - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
bookOverrides.why: ⚠️ Carries no series value at all — the trilogy name is inside the title. One of the two cases that prove a series-keyed lookup is insufficient; see `seriesToCreate` below and `_theHardPart`. Measured in site/catalog.csv 2026-08-11: series is blank on all three.

bookOverrides.title: Otherlife Nightmares - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
bookOverrides.why: ⚠️ Carries no series value at all — the trilogy name is inside the title. See `seriesToCreate`. Volume 2 is publication order, not alphabetical.

bookOverrides.title: Otherlife Awakenings - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
bookOverrides.why: ⚠️ Carries no series value at all — the trilogy name is inside the title. See `seriesToCreate`. Volume 3 despite sorting first alphabetically, which is how it currently sorts and is wrong.

seriesToCreate.name: The Selfless Hero Trilogy
seriesToCreate.why: ⚠️ All three Otherlife books carry the series name INSIDE their title and have no series field, so they read as three unrelated standalones. Grouping them is a fix to the audiobook catalog's data, not to this list — recorded here so the universe entry does not have to name three loose books forever.
seriesToCreate.note: Reading order is Dreams, Nightmares, Awakenings — NOT alphabetical, which is how they currently sort.

universes.confirmed: Owner confirmed 2026-08-11, after reviewing the full list, with three held out for verification.

universes.name: CAL Verse
universes.notes: Krout's shared world. Chance Encounter, Cooking with Disaster, Damsels of Distress, Full Murderhobo and Year of the Sword are also his and NOT included — unconfirmed, so left out rather than swept in.
universes.confirmed: Owner, 2026-08-11: 'everything Krout has written to this point that is a litrpg has been tied to the CAL Verse so for now, group them all together. I can tell you if we need to ungroup them later.' Grouped broadly by instruction; over-inclusion is accepted and reversible.
universes.evidence: Artorian's Archives is the strongest evidence in the whole list and it comes from the owner's own catalog, not recall: every volume is literally subtitled 'A Divine Dungeon Series' — Alumni, Anima, Annex, Axiom.
watch: Damsels of Distress — fairy-tale retellings; the least obviously LitRPG of the nine and the first candidate to ungroup.
Wolfman Warlock — co-authored with James Hunter, same caution as Turncoat's Truth.

seriesToFix.why: ⚠️ The m4b `trkn` TAGS were correct on all 14; the FILENAMES were the unreliable source. Untapped's filename says Book 11 while its tag says 12 — Goodreads confirms 12. Implode's filename carries no series at all while its tag knows both the series and track 8. So there was never a volume-11 collision, and the sweep does NOT need to reconstruct ordering. The only damaged field is the album/series string: four spellings, one of them ('Uncapped') holding the title instead of the series.
seriesToFix.alsoCheck: 'Invent' (audio) and 'Invent Short Story' (library) are probably the same book under two names.
seriesToFix.order: 1 Ritualist, 2 Regicide, 3 Rexus: Side Quest, 4 Raze, 5 Ruthless, 6 Inflame, 7 Invent, 7.75 Invent Short Story (assigned), 8 Implode, 9 Tenacity, 10 Thesaurize, 11 Thunderplump, 12 Untapped, 13 Unmapped, 14 Uncapped

assignedIndex.title: Invent Short Story
assignedIndex.why: ⚠️ ASSIGNED, not official. A Patreon exclusive, so it is unlisted on Goodreads and no canonical index exists. 6.5 and 7.5 already flank Invent, so 7.75 sorts after both and before Implode without colliding. Measured 12,029 words / ~44 pages against Krout novels of 116k-176k, which is what settles it as a genuine short story rather than a mislabelled copy of Invent.

notThisSeries.title: World's Only Hero
notThisSeries.why: the library files it there; the audio row is seriesless

collectsCases.title: The Divine Dungeon Complete Series
collectsCases.why: 564k words / ~2,053 pages — an OMNIBUS of all five Dungeon books, not a sixth book. Same shape as White Sand; belongs in edition.collects.

universes.name: Maasverse
series: A Court of Thorns and Roses
universes.notes: Canon, not fan inference: Crescent City book 2 (House of Sky and Breath) has an explicit, plot-critical ACOTAR crossover, carried further in House of Flame and Shadow. 19 rows across 3 series, all audiobooks — none in the library catalog.
dataProblems: ⚠️ ACOTAR's 11 rows are inflated. Duplicates: A Court of Thorns and Roses x3, A Court of Wings and Ruin x3, A Court of Mist and Fury x2. Some are legitimately different recordings (dramatized full-cast editions) but 11 is not 11 distinct books.
Part-files sit alongside their whole counterparts: 'A Court of Silver Flames (2 of 2)' and 'A Court of Wings and Ruin (1 of 3) []' — note the stray brackets in the latter.
Throne of Glass has 5 of 8 plus The Assassin's Blade — Empire of Storms, Tower of Dawn and Kingdom of Ash are genuine gaps, not data problems.

universes.name: Riordanverse
series: From the World of Percy Jackson
universes.notes: Camp Half-Blood continuity. 'From the World of Percy Jackson' is Sun and the Star, the Nico di Angelo novel co-written with Mark Oshiro — same continuity, found during review rather than in the first proposal.
universes.confirmed: Owner approved 2026-08-11, including the third series found during review.
watch: ⚠️ The ONLY universe spanning both catalogs. 13 Percy Jackson rows are 5 library (the Illumicrate exclusives) + 8 audio, and the five OVERLAP — the same books in two formats, not 13 titles. Counting them needs the catalogs reconciled, not summed.

⚠️ MORE PHYSICAL COPIES ARE COMING — the owner has a lot more Percy Jackson to scan. This is the first place the x2 'owned more than once' mark will legitimately fire, since today's five candidates were all children's books. It is also the free case for auto-assign: a known series mapping means every future scan lands in the universe with zero lookups.

Naming: the audio row 'Percy Jackson & the Olympians - The Demigod Files' uses '&' where every other row uses 'and'. A corrections-layer job — exactly the class of drift that splits a series under a text key, like the four Completionist Chronicles spellings.

universes.name: Solaria
universes.notes: Peckham and Valenti's shared realm. Structural rather than a cameo: Ruthless Boys of the Zodiac (the Dark Fae books) runs in PARALLEL with Zodiac Academy in Solaria, sharing characters and timeline, and the two are usually read interleaved. A stronger link than Maasverse, where one crossover scene does the work.
universes.naming: Named for the in-world realm rather than 'Zodiac Academy universe', which would elevate one series over the other — the same reason Divine Dungeon became CAL Verse.
dataProblems: ⚠️ Zodiac Academy has no consistent index: 'Zodiac Academy 8' and 'Zodiac Academy 8.5: Beyond the Veil' are numbered while everything else is titled.
Side stories sit inline with the main run: Live and Let Lionel, The Awakening as Told by the Boys, Origins of an Academy Bully, The Big A.S.S. Party.
'Zodiac Academy 2 - Ruthless Fae' carries its volume in the title — and is Ruthless FAE, not the separate Ruthless BOYS series.

universes.name: Willverse
universes.notes: Will Wight's shared multiverse. Each series is a distinct world — an 'Iteration' — and they are connected by the Way, a branching river of reality monitored by the Abidan Court. Cradle and The Last Horizon (Iteration 119, Fathom) are the two the household owns; The Elder Empire and The Traveler's Gate are listed so a future purchase files itself.
universes.confirmed: Owner approved 2026-08-12, and it was REFUSED twice before that on purpose. First pass: 'Will wight leave blank for now' — the author had only hinted. Second pass: the named continuity was established but the owner appeared to hold just ONE member series, and a universe covering one series says nothing the series name does not. It qualified only once The Last Horizon was confirmed as Iteration 119, giving it two owned series to span.
universes.evidence: The owner, 2026-08-12: 'each of Wight's series, including Cradle, Traveler's Gate, and Elder Empire, takes place on a different Iteration (a distinct universe) connected by a metaphysical network called the Way', and 'last horizon is connected... Iteration 119 (Fathom), a distinct world within Will Wight's shared multiverse'.
universes.naming: 'Willverse' follows this list's own convention — Maasverse, Riordanverse, Runnerverse — and is the word the owner's own source used. The in-world name for the connecting network is 'the Way', and the worlds are 'Iterations'; neither is the right shelf label, because the Way is the mechanism rather than the setting. Renaming is an owner decision and a guarded one: `canonicalNames` and `_pinnedCanonicalNames` exist so a rename cannot happen by accident.
watch: ⚠️ Holdings are 12 Cradle (ebook) + 3 The Last Horizon (3 audio, 3 library rows). NOT a 15-title universe if the two catalogs are ever summed — the same reconciliation trap Riordanverse carries.
The Elder Empire and The Traveler's Gate are claimed but NOT owned. They exist here so a future scan files itself with zero lookups; they should not be read as holdings.

_refused.subject: Children's picture-book lines — Bizzy Bear, Brown Bear and Friends, Baby University, The Pigeon, Elephant and Piggie, First 100
_refused.why: A brand or an imprint, not a fictional continuity. This is the LOUDEST possible false positive here: the library catalog is mostly children's books, so a rule that fires on these would bury the real answers.

_refused.subject: Same author, different world
_refused.why: Reckoners and the Cosmere share an author and nothing else. Author is not a universe.

_refused.subject: Turncoat's Truth — William D. Arand with Victor E. Krabin
_refused.why: Owner's call, 2026-08-11: 'Turncoat leave out for now while I verify.' Co-authored, and co-authored work does not always sit inside an author's shared continuity. Held out rather than swept in with the other 14 series.
_refused.heldOutSeriesEvidence: Exact series value measured in site/catalog.csv 2026-08-11, on "Turncoat's Truth - Turncoat's Truth, Book 1", authors 'William D. Arand, Victor E. Krabin'.
_refused.overturned: 2026-08-12: fully overturned — "Turncoat's Truth" restored into Runnerverse. Owner confirmed 2026-08-12: it IS in the Runnerverse. Held out on 2026-08-11 ('Turncoat leave out for now while I verify') because it is co-authored with Victor E. Krabin, and a collaboration does not reliably sit inside an author's own continuity — the same rule that keeps The Reckoners out of the Cosmere. The owner verified and it does.

_refused.subject: Cultivating Chaos and The Axe Falls — William D. Arand
_refused.why: Owner's call: 'Cultivating and axe falls should be excluded until I can verify.' ⚠️ Both are SINGLE-BOOK series, so there is no internal evidence of a shared world — only the author, and author alone is never sufficient here. That is the same reasoning that keeps Reckoners out of the Cosmere.
_refused.heldOutSeriesEvidence: ⚠️ Both measured in site/catalog.csv 2026-08-11, and the second one is NOT spelled the way the refusal reads: the series value is 'The Axe Falls Series', not 'The Axe Falls'. The book is 'The Axe Falls - The Axe Falls Series, Book 1'. Cultivating Chaos is 'Cultivating Chaos - VeilVerse: Cultivating Chaos, Book 1', series 'Cultivating Chaos' — note the row title mentions a 'VeilVerse', which is the sort of hint that is NOT evidence and is exactly what the owner is holding this back to verify.

_refused.subject: Tailored Realities — Brandon Sanderson
_refused.why: Believed to be a short-fiction collection, which would make it a mixed bag rather than a clean yes or no. Flagged rather than guessed, same treatment as Will Wight.
_refused.heldOutSeriesEvidence: It is a TITLE, not a series — measured in site/catalog.csv 2026-08-11: one row 'Tailored Realities', Brandon Sanderson, series blank. So it is held out as a title, which is why it uses heldOutTitles.

_shapeNotes.note: A universe flag belongs on the WORK, never on the edition
_shapeNotes.why: An omnibus is one object holding several works, and nothing stops a bind-up collecting works from different universes. Firstborn / Defending Elysium does not bite — neither novella is Cosmere — but a Cosmere-plus-non-Cosmere bind-up would make an edition-level flag simply wrong. edition.collects records what is inside; the universe answers per work.

_shapeNotes.note: Every edit goes through tools/universes.mjs, never a text editor
_shapeNotes.why: The CLI refuses an addition that carries no reason. Hand-editing the JSON is the one way to land a bare mapping, which destroys the property that makes this file worth keeping — that every entry says how it was decided and on what evidence. Run `node tools/universes.mjs validate` after any hand edit anyway; it is what CI-equivalent checks in both catalogs run.

_shapeNotes.note: Consumers hold this in memory; nothing queries it
_shapeNotes.why: Six universes, ~33 series, ~13 book overrides. library_catalog materialises a gitignored copy at build time and bundles it into the Worker; audiobook_catalog reads it from disk during the Python build. Neither writes to it — writes happen here, through the CLI, in a commit.

_changelogDoc: Every mutation made through tools/universes.mjs, newest last. Git records WHAT changed; this records WHY a thing was removed, which a deleted line cannot.

_changelog.why: Owner confirmed 2026-08-12: it IS in the Runnerverse. Held out on 2026-08-11 ('Turncoat leave out for now while I verify') because it is co-authored with Victor E. Krabin, and a collaboration does not reliably sit inside an author's own continuity — the same rule that keeps The Reckoners out of the Cosmere. The owner verified and it does.
